column1: # with sdk- are rewritten by tools/symbols/match_libs.py. Add your own with the source user. The
# type is a C type from game/types.h or the SDK's headers, and the comment goes above the global.

column5: The id of Kamui's last texture DMA request, which kmyCopyToTexture writes. kmQueryFinishLastTextureDMA and so njLoadTextureFinishDMA check whether it has finished.

The GD file system's directory buffer with room for 1,024 entries, which the system setup (FUN_8c056748) gives gdFsInit2. The same address is also the top of the 0x5000-byte stack from 0x8C124CC0, which the setup gives syHwInit and syFbrInitEx.
The GD file system's work area for up to 8 open files, which the system setup (FUN_8c056748) gives gdFsInit2. The setup aligns 0x8C134CF0 up to 32 bytes to get it.
The peripheral library's send buffer, which the system setup (FUN_8c056748) gives pdInitPeripheral. The setup aligns 0x8C136084 up to 32 bytes to get it.
The peripheral library's receive buffer, which the system setup (FUN_8c056748) gives pdInitPeripheral. The setup aligns 0x8C1420A4 up to 32 bytes to get it.

1 while no write to the memory card runs: gameMain sets it before gameInit, saveWrite sets it to 0 when buSaveFile starts, and saveWriteDone sets it to 1 again. gameMain does not end its loop while it is 0, and gameTaskFrame takes a soft reset back to the title only while it is 1.
The 0x80000-byte buffer that gameMain allocates for the texture loads from the disc and gives textureBufferSet. gameMain frees it at the end.
The 0x480 texture system records (NJS_TEXSYSTEM, 40 bytes each) that gameMain allocates and gives njInitTextureEx. gameMain frees them at the end.
The 0x480 texture management records (NJS_TEXMANAGE, 24 bytes each) that gameMain allocates and gives njInitTextureEx. gameMain frees them at the end.
The buffer for 0x1000 vertices (NJS_VERTEX_BUF, 64 bytes each) that gameMain allocates and gives njInit3D. gameMain frees it at the end.
The 32 matrices of Ninja's matrix stack, which gameMain allocates and gives njInitMatrix. gameMain frees them at the end.

The setup of Ninja's vertex buffer, which gameMain fills and gives njCalcVertexBufferSize and njInitVertexBufferEx: nTextureMemorySize 0x80000, 0x400 textures, 0x80 small VQ textures and one pass, whose 5 list sizes are -1, 0x40000, 0x80000, 0x40000 and 0x40000. gameMain allocates the buffer (pVertexBuffer, this label) at the size from njCalcVertexBufferSize (nVertexBufferSize, 0x8C1520E4) and frees it at the end.

The head of the list of objects to destroy at the program's end, each entry a next pointer, a destructor and an object, which staticDestructorsRun takes from it. No other code refers to it, so it keeps its start value 0 and the list stays empty.

The size in bytes of textureBuffer, rounded down to whole sectors of 2,048 bytes. textureBufferSet sets it and textureBufferGet returns it. textureLoad and textureStepOpen read at most this size in sectors at once, and paletteFileLoad gives it to fileReadToBuffer as the size of the buffer.

The work buffer for loading files from the disc, which textureBufferSet sets and textureBufferGet returns. gameMain gives it textureReadBuffer. textureLoad, paletteFileLoad and textureStepOpen (for textureStepRead) get it and read texture and palette files into it.
The start of the PVM archive in memory that pvmReadBegin sets. pvmSeek with mode 0 moves the read position (pvmPosition) to it plus an offset.

The read position in the PVM archive in memory. pvmReadBegin sets it to the start, pvmRead returns it and moves it on by a size, and pvmSeek moves it from the start (mode 0) or from where it is (mode 1).
Never written, so always 0. A step of textureLoadStep copies it to the flag at 0x8C0CF7E4 when it waits, ends or fails, which ends textureLoadStep's loop for this call.
The disc file of the texture that textureLoadStep loads. textureStepOpen opens it, and the steps close it when the load ends or fails.
1 when the texture that textureLoadStep loads is PVR data in memory (attribute 0x40000000), 0 when it comes from a file. textureStepCheck sets it, and the later steps close textureFile only at 0.
The texture list that textureLoadStep loads from, which it keeps at its first step.
The list's entry of the texture that textureLoadStep loads: its file name, or its PVR data in memory, and its attributes.
The index in textureLoadList of the texture that textureLoadStep loads. The steps copy it to 0x8C10B38C on an error.

The texture's number in Ninja's texture management, which njEntryTextureManageNum gives at step 7. textureStepUpload loads the parts into it, and a failed upload or DMA releases it (njReleaseTextureManageNum).

The PVR header of the texture that textureLoadStep loads, which njLoadPvrHeader reads from the file's first part or from memory. For memory data without a header, textureStepMemoryHeader fills the type and the width and height (0x8C15C4C0, 0x8C15C4C2) from the entry's data at 4, 0x10 and 0x14.
The size in sectors of the texture's file, which textureStepOpen gets (gdFsGetFileSctSize).
The size of textureStepBuffer in sectors of 2048 bytes, the most sectors that textureStepRead reads at once.

The sectors of the texture's file still to read. textureStepOpen sets the file's size, textureStepRead takes off each read, and it is 0 for a texture in memory. textureStepWaitDma ends the load when it is below 1, else reads on.

The bytes of the texture already loaded into texture memory, the offset of the next part (njLoadTexturePart). textureStepUpload adds each part's size. At 0 after a read, textureStepWaitRead goes on to the PVR header (step 5), else to the upload (step 8).
The size in bytes of the part that textureStepUpload loads next: the bytes of the last read, less the PVR header for the first part, or the whole texture (njCalcTextureSize2) for one in memory.
The address of the data of the part that textureStepUpload loads next: textureStepBuffer after a read, past the PVR header for the first part, or the texture's data in memory.
The calls of textureStepWaitDma that found the texture's DMA unfinished. At 11 the load fails with error 1. textureStepUpload sets it to 0.
The calls of textureStepWaitRead that found the disc read still busy. Past 1000 the load fails with error 5. textureStepRead sets it to 0.
The step loader's copy of the work buffer that textureBufferGet returns, which textureStepOpen gets with its size (textureStepBufferSize). textureStepRead reads the file's sectors into it.
The size in bytes of textureStepBuffer, which textureStepOpen gets from textureBufferGet and divides into sectors (textureBufferSectors).
The last result of textureLoadStep in textureListLoadStep: 0 while it works, 1 when done and -1 on an error. Nothing reads it.
The function of the current step, which textureLoadStep takes from the table at 0x8C0CF7F4 by textureStep and calls.
The texture of the list that textureListLoadStep loads, 0 at first. It moves to the next when one is done, and goes back to 0 after the last one, on an error and at textureLoadStop.

The state of textureLoadStep: 0 idle, 1 textureStepCheck, 2 textureStepOpen, 3 textureStepRead, 4 textureStepWaitRead, 5 textureStepFileHeader, 6 textureStepMemoryHeader, 7 textureStepEntry, 8 textureStepUpload and 9 textureStepWaitDma. Each step sets the next, and the end or an error sets 0.
The game's copies of the two controllers, made each frame by gameReadPad.
Shinobi's records of the two controllers.
Each player's frames since the player joined: playerJoin sets it to 0, and gameTaskFrame adds 1 to both at each frame that no player holds the pause, as it does to gameFrames. Nothing reads it.
Each player's joined mark: playerJoin sets it to 1, and gameInit and playerJoinedClear set it to 0xFF. Only playerJoinedClear reads it.

1 from a new game's start (gameNewInit) until playTimeAdd adds the game's time, which then sets it to -1. playTimeAdd adds nothing while it is negative, as after gameInit (0xFF), so a game's time counts once. At 1, titleTask's state 13 shows the credits for 127 frames (creditsShowTime) when it requests the next scene.

The frames whose task lists ran outside the pause: gameTaskFrame adds 1 after it runs lists 0 to 5. Effects blink and cycle by its low bits. gameInit sets it to 0 and demoStart to the value in the demo's record.

1 when VIEW RANKING in the RANKING menu (rankingMenu) asks for the ranking scene. With it or rankingAfterGame set, sceneRankingStart makes the ranking wait for input instead of the attract demo's turns, and then sets it back to 0.

1 when the ranking scene follows a game, which gameOverTask, endingFinish and endingTrialUpdate set. sceneRankingStart then keeps the game's difficulty and gameTwoPlayers, and rankingUpdate shows the play data first (rankingPlayData) and sets it back to 0.
The frames without a press on either controller while idleDarken is set. Past 10800 gameFrame darkens the screen (idleDarkened). A press and the screens that set idleDarken reset it to 0.
The alpha of the black over the darkened screen (idleDarkened). gameFrame starts it at 0 and raises it by 2 at each frame up to 200, and gameTaskFrame draws it (screenDarken).

1 where the screen darkens after 10800 frames without a press (gameFrame): the title's menus, the pause menu and the ranking while it waits for input. gameEnterScene, the main menu's return to the attract mode and the end of the pause set it to 0.

1 while the screen is darkened for want of input. gameFrame sets it past 10800 idle frames, and gameTaskFrame then draws the black (screenDarken with idleDarkenAlpha). gameReadPad gives the game empty pads until a press, which sets it back to 0.

The frames that creditsDraw still shows the credits. The pause outside the tutorial and the mode select hold it at 31, and a join, a continue or a new game from the title set it to 127. creditsDraw counts it down and fades the text out below 31. Holding X and Y in the pause, sceneTitleStart and pauseRestart set it to 0.
The scene that runs: 1 boot, 2 logos, 3 rankings (sceneRankingStart), 4 title, 5 mode select, 6 to 10 the chapters, 11 tutorial, 12 ending.
The scene to change to at the next frame, 0 for none.

The players whom the stage keeps from joining, a bit each: the ship sequences, the results, the remain bonus, chapter 1's opening flight and the tutorial set 3 for both. The ship sequences' and the results' updates, ch1IntroEnd, the chapters' starts, gameInit and gameNewInit set 0. While a player's bit is set here or in playersOut, playerJoinCheck ignores the player's Start, playerDraw holds a joined ship in state 5 and hudPressStart shows its wait text.

The players who cannot join yet, a bit each: playerUpdate sets a player's bit when the last ship is lost, and gameOverCheck sets both at the game over. continueTask clears the bit when the player continues or when the count runs out without a game over, and continueEnd clears it when the continue's task ends otherwise. playerJoinCheck, playerDraw and hudPressStart treat it as joinLocked.

1 while a bank load over frames loads a texture list in steps (textureListLoadStep), in modelFileLoad and bankLoadStep. loadsAbort then stops the texture load (textureLoadStop) and mounts the disc again.

1 while bankLoadStep loads a bank, which keeps another bank's load from starting until then (bankLoadStep returns 1 for it). bankLoadStep sets it back to 0 when the bank is loaded, and loadsAbort clears it.

1 while a boss's destruction flashes the fade (bossDeathUpdate). On a horizontal screen fadeDraw then draws the fade's quad turned by polygonTurn instead of turning the clipping off and drawing it unturned. gameEnterScene clears it.

The blending flags of the fade's quad, which fadeDraw gives spriteMode: 0 alpha blending, 0x1000000 additive. The flashes of bossDeathUpdate and ch5EndUpdate set 0x1000000, and gameEnterScene, gameOverCheck, resultsStep, stageUpdate and tutFadeOut set 0.
The number of objects of the model that modelNodeTreeCreate makes a tree for, which modelNodeCount counts. modelNodeTreeCreate allocates a node of 0x14 bytes for each.
The index of the next free node while modelNodeTreeFill fills a new tree, which modelNodeTreeCreate sets to 0.
1 holds the fade: fadeTo makes no task and fadeStop removes none. gameOverCheck sets it once it starts the game over's fade to black, and fadeReset clears it.

1 while a fade task (fadeTask) moves the fade's corners. A new fade task waits until it is 0 before it starts, and fadeStop and fadeReset clear it. The mode select, the rankings, the ending and ch5EndUpdate wait for it to be 0 before they go on.
The level of Ninja's fade, which fadeLevelSet sets. fogFadeApply passes it to njExecuteFade each frame while fogFadeOn is set and fogFadeMode is 1.

Which effect fogFadeApply and drawFog use while fogFadeOn is set: 0 Ninja's fog with the fog table at 0x8C1CAC88, 1 Ninja's fade at ninjaFadeLevel. fogReset and most scenes' light and fog functions set 0, and modeSelectLightFog and ch1FadeLevelIn set 1. fogFadeOff turns off the effect that it names.

1 while the fog or Ninja's fade applies: the scenes' light and fog functions (ch1LightFog1, modeSelectLightFog and others) set it, and fogFadeOff clears it. While it is set, fogFadeApply applies them each frame and drawFog turns them on or off for each draw.

The number of extra point lights added this frame (lightAdd), up to 4, as lights 3 to 6 of the multi-light models. lightsExtraClear sets it to 0, and lightsApply picks the multi-light models' light set by it plus 2 (FUN_8c01a2c8, FUN_8c029838).

The main light's angle about x, which lightAim uses with lightAngleY to turn lightDirection. It is the first of the 13 light values that lightsReset, lightsMix, lightsFadeTo and the scenes' light functions set: the two angles, lightColor, lightIntensity, lightAmbient, multiLightColor and multiLightAmbient.
The main light's angle about y, which lightAim uses with lightAngleX to turn lightDirection.

The main light's direction, the vector (0, 0, -1) that lightAim turns by the view's angles and the light's two angles. lightsApply gives it to the Easy and Simple models' light (FUN_8c019ca4, FUN_8c01c65c) and as the direction of light 1 of the multi-light models.
The main light's red, green and blue, which lightsApply gives to the Easy and Simple models (FUN_8c019cc0, njCnkSetSimpleLightColor). lightsReset sets 1, 1, 1, and ch1LightColor sets 0.8, 0.56, 0.4.
The main light's intensity, 1 by default (lightsReset), which lightsApply gives to the Easy and Simple models with lightAmbient (FUN_8c019cb2, FUN_8c01c66a).
The ambient light of the Easy and Simple models, 0.25 by default (lightsReset), which lightsApply gives with lightIntensity.
The red, green and blue of light 1 of the multi-light models, whose direction lightsApply sets to lightDirection (FUN_8c01a330, FUN_8c0298a0). lightsReset sets 1, 1, 1.
The ambient light of the multi-light models, red, green and blue, which lightsApply gives them (FUN_8c01a322, FUN_8c029892). lightsReset sets 0.24 each.

The sound library's memory block that soundInit makes (sdMemBlkCreate). soundLoadBanks points it at each loaded file of a bank list (sdMemBlkSetPrm) and sends the file to the driver through it, with sdBankDownload or, for an entry of type 0, with FUN_8c051194.

Each player's 11 counters of the name entry's button repeat, one for each button of the table at 0x8C0D0B8C (the four directions, Start, A, B, C, X, Y and Z). padRepeatUpdate sets a counter to 0 while its button is up and raises it while the button is held. The button fires at 0 and at 15, where the counter goes back to 14. padRepeatReset clears both players' counters.
The text that hudPressStart picks and draws for its blinking line: GAME OVER, PRESS START, PLEASE WAIT, PRESS START BUTTON or PRESS START TO SKIP. Only hudPressStart uses it.

playersInGame as playersKeep kept it at the tutorial's start (stageStart in scene 11), which playersRestore gives back. In a trial game stageDraw lets only the Start of these players leave the tutorial.
gamePrototype as playersKeep kept it at the tutorial's start, which playersRestore gives back.

The PRACTICE menu's cursor while the menu is closed, 5 times the difficulty plus the chapter from 0. titleMenuReset and a change of DIFFICULTY in configMenu set it to the first chapter of optionDifficulty (0 with USER SELECT). practiceMenu keeps menuItem in it when a chapter is picked and when the menu is left on a chapter, and mainMenu starts PRACTICE's cursor from it.
The scene that follows the stage, which each chapter's start and the tutorial's start set. stageCmdEnd and the tutorial's exit in stageDraw change to it.
The 7 task lists, each its first and last task.
Set to 1 when the disc tray opens, when gameFrame returns nonzero, or at a controller reset in the attract mode or in scene 1. gameMain's loop then ends, but not while a save is being written.
MONITOR TYPE: 1 for the two horizontal types, 0 for the two vertical ones. optionsApply copies it to screenHorizontal, and saveCalcSum sums the save block from this byte on.
1: gameReadPad turns the pads' directions a quarter turn (left to down, right to up, up to left, down to right). The config menu sets it only with a vertical monitor type.
AUTO SAVE: 1, gameEnterScene writes the save to the card when saveRequest is set. The backup menu toggles it, and a failed save sets it to 0.
1: the horizontal screen at 75%, 0: at 80%.

Four bits that open the appendix menu's items: 0x2 the first gallery, 0x1 the second gallery, 0x4 the sound test and 0x8 the game mode choice. The ending sets 0x1 for a clear, 0x4 or 0x8 for a clear without continues at easy or normal, 0x2 for a trial clear without continues, and playTimeAdd sets 0x2, 0x1, 0x4 and 0x8 after 5, 10, 15 and 20 hours of play.
1: the prototype mode, in which shots cost energy.
Set: the next scene change saves to the card, with optionAutosave on.
Each player's spare lives, without the ship in play. playerStart sets gameLives - 1, scoreAdd adds one at extendScore, and a ship lost at 0 puts the player out.
The player who joined last (playerJoin), 0 or 1. With one player rankingPlayDataDraw shows this player's scores and chains (chapterScores).

The frames left in the current count of the continue: continueStart sets 127, and stageDraw counts it down, plays the count's sound at 120 (continueCountSound) and at 0 lowers continueTimer and sets 127 again. continueScreen sets it to 0 on A or B below 120, and the continue runs out once it and continueTimer are 0.

Each player's frames of GAME OVER in the player's place of the HUD, 127 when the player's continue runs out while the game goes on (continueTask) or its task is removed before its end (continueEnd). hudPressStart counts it down and shows GAME OVER while it is not 0, and playerStart sets it to 0.

The players whose ship was hit with no spare life and is still dying, a bit each. playerUpdate sets the bit at the hit and clears it when it puts the player out (playerOut). scoreAdd gives such a player no points, gameOverCheck waits until it is 0, and rankingFindPlaces with two players finds no place while the other player's bit is set.

1 in chapter 5's last fight: ch5FinalCreate sets it, and stageStart clears it with the 20 bytes from stageLocks. While it is set, playerAbsorb gives score but no energy, hudDraw draws no energy, and playerOut stores no chapter scores (chapterScoresStore).

The stage's scroll, the position along the stage's path that pathAt reads. stageUpdate adds scrollSpeed each frame and stops it at the path's end, and stage commands and scripts wait until it reaches their positions.
The scroll's speed, a float, which moves toward scrollTarget.
The input of the recorded entry that demoInputRead plays now, with bit 0x80 cleared, which it gives the ship as its held input. stageStart clears it.

The frames that the current entry of the recorded input still plays after this one: demoInputRead takes the entry's count, lowers it each frame and reads the next entry at 0. demoStart and stageStart clear it.

The bytes left in the recorded input of a demo or the tutorial, which demoStart sets from word 4 of the demo's record and stageStart clears. demoInputRead takes one or two bytes for each input change and gives no input once it is 0.

Each player's flag, 1 while the ship has not shot or released since playerScoresClear set it (gameNewInit, playerStart), and playerButtons clears it at a shot or a release. resultsPlayRank gives the chapter play rank 0x0C to one player in the game whose flag is set, or 0x0D to two players only when both are set. rankingAdd keeps it in byte 7 of the ranking entry.

Each player's count of chapters that resultsPlayRank gave the no-shot rank (playerNoShot). rankingPlayDataDraw blinks You're Real DOT-EATER! when it reaches 5 with one player, or DOT-EATERS! when both reach 5 with two. playerScoresClear sets it to 0.
Each player's score.
The fade's four corners, a polygon over the whole screen.

The red of the fog's color, 0 to 255, the first value of the fog's stored setting up to fogFadeLevel. The light and fog setups of the scenes set it and apply it (fogColorSet), fogFadeTask moves it to a target (fogMix), and fogFadeTo starts a fade from it.
The green of the fog's color, 0 to 255, which fogColorSet applies with fogRed and fogBlue.
The blue of the fog's color, 0 to 255, which fogColorSet applies with fogRed and fogGreen.
The fog's near depth in its stored setting, which fogTableSet applies with fogFar. The light and fog setups set it, and fogFadeTask moves it to a target (fogMix).
The fog's far depth in its stored setting, which fogTableSet applies with fogNear. The light and fog setups set it, fogFadeTask moves it to a target (fogMix), and ch1FogFarUpdate sets it each frame.
The level of Ninja's fade in the fog's stored setting, which fadeLevelSet applies. Most light and fog setups set and apply it, and fogFadeTask moves it to a target (fogMix).

The stage's offset of the camera in x, y and z, which stageUpdate copies to the camera's offset each frame. The stage programs set it to 0 at their start. ch3ShipsAUpdate eases x and y, and ch5EndUpdate and ch5ShipsUpdate ease y (easeFloat).

The stage's additions to the camera's 4 orbit angles, which stageUpdate adds to pathAngles and pathValue for the camera's orbit each frame. The stage programs set and ease them, and so do tasks of chapters 1, 2, 3 and 5 (easeWord). ch1Bg03Draw draws more of its background while [3] is outside -0x1800 to 0x1800.
The stage's distance of the camera's orbit, which stageUpdate copies to the camera each frame. The stage programs set and ease it, and ch5BossRoomUpdate eases it.
The stage's perspective for the flat view, an angle that stageUpdate copies to the camera's flatPerspective each frame. The stage programs set it to 11832, about 65 degrees.
The stage's depth for the camera, a float that stageUpdate copies to the camera's depth as an int each frame. The stage programs set it at their start.
Each player's ship (Player).

Each player's directions and buttons in this frame, held and newly pressed: 1 up, 2 down, 4 left, 8 right, 0x10 shot, 0x20 switch, 0x40 release. playerReadInput makes it from the controller, demoInputRead from the recorded input.
Each player's energy for homing lasers: a release fires one laser for each 10, up to 12. It holds up to 120, or up to 999 in the prototype mode, where shots spend it too.
Each player's polarity, 0 or 1, which playerSetPolarity keeps and playerCreate gives the ship at the next stage start. playerStart sets it to 0.
Each player's shot button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonShot.
Each player's switch button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonSwitch.
Each player's release button: an index into buttonMasks, which playerJoin copies from optionButtonRelease.
Each player's setting that shot and switch pressed together release too.
The controller bits of the 7 button choices of the controller settings: A, B, R or C, X, Y, L or Z, and none.
The frames that hitPass waits before it plays the next hit sound: 4 after each sound, counted down each frame. hitStart sets it to 0.
The priority of the pending hit sound, 0 for none or 1 to 3, which hitSoundRequest raises. hitPass plays sound 0x11, 0x10 or 0x0F for priority 1, 2 or 3 at hitSoundPosition and sets it to 0.
The position of the pending hit sound: x and y from hitSoundRequest, and z, which only hitStart sets (to 0). hitPass plays the sound there.
The next free entry of the room for 2048 filed hit records (HitFiled) at 0x8C1D1590, which hitListsClear resets each frame. hitFile fills it and moves it on when it files a record.

The next free place of the sphere buffer, room for 2048 spheres (NJS_SPHERE) at 0x8C1DF594, which hitListsClear resets each frame. hitShapePlace and hitShapeTransform write the placed spheres of the filed records there.
The number of members in each of the 4 script groups.
The 4 stage script groups, up to 256 members each, which a record can wait to be empty.
Each player's current set of kills: its color in the high 4 bits and its kills in the low 4.
Each player's chain: the completed sets of three kills of one color in a row.
Each player's longest chain in this stage. stageStart clears it, and chapterScoresStore keeps it for the chapter.
Each player's score for the next extra life.
The game's EXTEND, which optionsApply copies from optionExtend. playerStart and scoreAdd read it.
The 200 objects that homing lasers can aim at, with where each was drawn and the damage on its way to it.
This frame's hit records, in 5 lists: ships, fields, shots, enemies and bullets.
The laser slot of the object hit this frame, whose hit points the gauge shows.
The players in the game, a bit each: 0x01 player 1, 0x02 player 2. playerStart sets a player's bit, and a hit with no spare life clears it.
1 in the prototype mode.
The pause: 1 paused, 2 to pause at the next frame.

The players who hold the pause, a bit each. pauseUpdate sets it to 1 or 2 for the player who pressed Start, and the pause menu clears a player's bit. At 0 the pause menu ends the pause, and gameTaskFrame counts gameFrames only while it is 0.
A 1 here ends the pause.
1 while the pause holds the sound.

The players who cannot pause, a bit each. gameEnterScene locks both, a chapter's start unlocks the players in the game, joining or continuing unlocks a player, and losing the last ship or going out locks the player again.

1 in the attract mode: set after the boot's card check, at the end of a game and when the main menu is left, and cleared by Start on the title. The demos, the logos and the title before Start run with it.
What happened in this frame, cleared by stageUpdate: 0x02 the bullets vanish.
The speed that the scroll moves toward.
How much the scroll's speed moves toward its target in a frame.
The read position in the recorded input of a demo or the tutorial, which demoStart sets and stageStart clears. While it is not 0, demoInputRead gives player 1's ship this input instead of the pad's.

The stage's lock bytes: command 2 raises the first, command 3 waits until stageUnlock lowers it to 0, command 4 waits for any byte from here to be 0, and the ease commands hold one as their task's lock. stageStart clears 20 bytes from here, which also hold playersContinuing, nameEntryPlayers, gameOver and stageEvents.
A counter that stage command 3 raises. Command 6 and stageStart set it to 0.
A counter that the stage program raises (command 6).
The stage program's commands by number. See docs/game.md, The stage program.
1 in the practice mode, which returns to the title after the chapter.
The stage path's point at scrollPosition, from pathAt. The camera orbits about it, and the draws of objects on the path start from it.
The stage path's three angles at scrollPosition, from pathAt. stageUpdate adds them to the camera's orbit, and the draws on the path turn by them.
The path's seventh value at scrollPosition.
The camera's structure (Camera) while a camera task lives: the mode select, each stage, the ranking and the ending make one (cameraCreate).
The game's slot for each of the 8 sequence players (soundSequencePlayers): the sequence to play, its level and pan, and its state. soundServer starts, pauses and resumes the players from it.
The game's slot for each of the 20 one-shot players (soundEffectPlayers): the sound to play, its level and pan, and its state. soundServer starts, pauses and resumes the players from it.
The sound library's 8 MIDI sequence players.
The sound library's 20 one-shot players.
The 4 loaded lists of sound banks. Slot 0 holds SFX_DEFAULT.BIN's.
The file names of the sound bank lists.
1: no sound starts.
1: sounds get a pan and a volume from their position.
The game's difficulty: 0 easy, 1 normal, 2 hard.
The random numbers' state.
The data of the hit point gauge's task, which hpGaugeCreate makes at the stage start. hpGaugeSet puts the hit points of the object in gaugeSlot into it.
The save block's identifier, IK-BKUP 1.2.
The sum of the save block's other bytes (saveCalcSum).
TRIAL GAME: 1, GAME START goes to the mode select, which offers the trial game (gameTrial). The config menu toggles it, and it is 1 by default.
DIFFICULTY: 0 EASY, 1 NORMAL, 2 HARD, or 3 USER SELECT, which chooses at the mode select (difficultyChoice). optionsApply sets difficulty from it.
PLAYER STOCK: the lives at the start, 1 to 5 and 3 by default. optionsApply copies it to gameLives.
EXTEND: 0 none, 1 one every 2,000,000, 2 one at 3,000,000 and then every 5,000,000 more, 3 one at 6,000,000 and one at 15,000,000. optionsApply copies it to gameExtend.
Each player's shot button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, A by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonShot.
Each player's switch button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, B by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonSwitch.
Each player's release button in CONFIG, an index into buttonMasks (0 to 6, R or C by default). playerJoin copies it to buttonRelease.
Each player's setting in CONFIG that shot and switch pressed together release too, 1 by default. playerJoin copies it to buttonShotSwitch.
The HUD's offset in x, in steps of 4 from -28 to 12, which left and right change in the pause menu. hudPlace and the other HUD draws move the HUD by it, the other way for player 2.
The HUD's offset in y, in steps of 4 from -28 to 12, which up and down change in the pause menu. hudPlace and the other HUD draws move the HUD by it.
Each player's vibration, on or off.
The credits that sceneTitleStart gives a game, 3 at first. playTimeAdd adds one for each hour of play up to 9, and an hour after that sets 0xFF, free play.
For each difficulty, the highest chapter that a game reached without a continue, 1 at first. PRACTICE offers the chapters up to it.
The play time at which the next credit comes.
The seconds of play, up to 1,000 hours.

The rankings: 4 tables of 12 lists of 20 entries (RankEntry), which rankingDefaults fills. rankingFindPlaces and rankingAdd use the table of difficulty, lists 0 to 5 for one player and 6 to 11 for two.
The card file's header.
The card file's image while the card reads or writes it.
The game's PLAYER STOCK, which optionsApply copies from optionLives and demoStart takes from the demo's record. playerStart gives one less as spare lives.
The difficulty chosen at the mode select, in the practice menu or for the tutorial, 1 at power-on. While optionDifficulty is 3, optionsApply sets difficulty from it.
The credits left in this game. 0xFF: free play.
The frames since the game's start, without those while a player holds the pause (pausePlayer). playTimeAdd turns them into seconds of playTime.
The game's copy of optionHorizontal, which optionsApply makes. With 0, a vertical screen, screenPlace turns 2D positions a quarter turn and cameraFlat turns the view.
The game's copy of optionScreen75.
Each player's continues, up to 255. A player who joins starts with it as the score, up to 9.
This game's place in each of the 6 ranking lists, 0xFF for none.
1 once both players are in the game.

Three blocks of 6 entries, each a score and a longest chain, for player 1, player 2 and both players together (chapterScoresTotal), with the game's total in entry 0 and each chapter's part in entries 1 to 5. rankingFindPlaces compares them with ranking lists 0 to 5, or for two players with lists 6 to 11.
The disc's directories that fileSetDir changes to.
The file that the disc reads now.
Where the disc read goes.
The size of the file that the disc reads.
The 16 graphics banks (Bank): models, sprites and a texture list each.

Room for 128 scenery polygons (SceneryPolygon), an origin and a polygon each. sceneryAdd adds them during a frame, sceneryClear empties them each frame, and sceneryHit tests the ships, shots, lasers and bullets against them.
The number of polygons in sceneryPolygons.
The state of the VMU screen in the first socket of each controller (ports A1 and B1): 0 none, 1 to 8 what to show, 9 writing it. vmuScreenEvent picks what to show, and vmuScreenUpdate runs it.
1 in a trial game.
1 in a game that enters no ranking: a practice or a trial.
The players at the name entry.
The frames since gameInit.
The players at the continue, a bit each.
Each player's 1 once a join counts as a continue.
The continue's countdown, from 9.
1 once the game over runs.

The boss's state, which bossStateSet sets: 0xFF from stageStart, 0 once the stage program reaches the boss, and 1 from the boss's task when the boss is destroyed. While it is 0, resultsStart gives no bonus for the boss time left. hudUpdate runs one of its moves only while it is not 0xFF.
The depth of the title's menu stack (menuStack), which menuPush raises, menuPop lowers and titleMenuReset sets to 0.
The title's menu stack, entries of 3 bytes up to menuItem: menuItem[0], menuItem[1] and titleState, which menuPush saves at menuDepth and menuPop restores.
The cursor of the title menu that runs. In the controller settings [0] is player 1's cursor and [1] player 2's.
The title's screen. See docs/game.md, The title and its menus.
The count of attract demos, which titlePressStart raises before each one. Its value mod 3 picks the demo: 0 the tutorial, 1 chapter 1, 2 chapter 2.
The seconds left on the boss timers whose bosses died in time, which bossTimeAdd sums and stageStart clears. The results pay 10,000 points for each second (BOSS DESTROY BONUS).
The seconds left on the boss's timer, in both halfwords: bossTimerUpdate writes both, and the HUD reads the upper one.

A count of requests for each of the 4 vibration units (sockets 1 and 2 of each controller), which vibrationStart raises. A vibration task whose count is no longer the current one ends without starting.
The data of ch1Bg00Create's task, whose first word holds the draw flags of its model. ch1Bg00Create sets them to 0 and ch1Bg00Flags changes them.

Chapter 3's lane speed, the distance that the chapter's objects move in a frame: ch3LanesPart1 sets -0.1 and ch3LanesPart2 -1. The lanes (ch3LaneUpdate) count their distances by it, and the chapter's walls, blocks, turrets and enemies add it to their positions or take it as their speed.

The data of chapter 3's mid-boss's task, which ch3MidBossCreate sets and ch3MidBossDestroy clears. A block of a ch3BlockRow (ch3RowBlockUpdate) explodes when the mid-boss at bytes 0x40 and 0x44 comes within 9.5 of it, and raises its byte 0x0C.

The centre of chapter 4's core on the play field, x, y and z, which ch4CoreDraw sets each frame (pointToPlane, z 0). The core's walls, bullets, laser points and the emitters' shots measure from it, and its sounds play at it.

The centre of the swing of chapter 4's core on the play field, x, y and z: the origin of the fortress's node 48, which ch4CoreDraw sets each frame (pointToPlane, z 0). ch4CoreWallsUpdate adds the core's round polygon to the scenery there, and ch4EmitterPlace places the emitters on a circle about it.

The turn of chapter 4's fortress as it moves to its places, an angle that ch4FortressUpdate eases on a cosine from 0 to 0x10000 and later from 0 to -0x10000. ch4SkyTurnDraw adds it to its angle about y, and ch4FortressCreate sets it to 0.
A pointer to the position of the object of chapter 5's last fight, at byte 0x68 of its data, which ch5FinalUpdate sets. The homing lasers of ch5End (ch5EndLaserUpdate) turn toward it.

The request for the closing ring of chapter 5's last fight. ch5EndUpdate sets it to 1 on its frame 40, and ch5FinalUpdate then makes the ring (ch5FinalRingClose) and sets it back to 0. ch5FinalCreate sets it to 0.
While not 0, the lit buttons of the tutorial's controller blink (tutPadDraw). tutPadBlink sets it for the tutorial's stage program.
The draws of the tutorial's controller, which tutPadDraw counts up. The lit buttons blink by its bit 0x02 while tutPadBlinkOn is set.
